meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_154_packages.json, all reference===154 edges from torahData.js (1 bechina edge, 3 eitza edges), and the full source text torah_154.txt (9 lines). For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset and whether it is assigned to a package. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, כְּנֶגֶד, הַיְנוּ, מְקוֹם) were considered. Torah #154 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan — it is largely a summary pointing back to Torah #15. The dataset is severely undergapped for this Torah.

additions.reason: The Torah opens with 'דַּע, כִּי יֵשׁ יִרְאוֹת נְפוּלוֹת' — the fallen fears. These are explicitly established as a bechina of the five primordial terrors ('הֵם בְּחִינַת חָמֵשׁ אֵימוֹת'). The fallen fears are the evil/fallen dimension of yirah — the upper fear that descended from its root and became clothed in worldly things, causing all sufferings and judgments. This is the negative pole of Package 1: the same yirah-force that in its elevated form is יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת becomes, when fallen, the cause of every kind of suffering. Polarity is evil because the fallen fears are the mechanism through which the klipa/evil operates on a person.
additions.source_quote: דַּע, כִּי יֵשׁ יִרְאוֹת נְפוּלוֹת, וְכָל הַיִּסּוּרִין וְהַדִּינִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם, כֻּלָּם הֵם מֵהַיִּרְאוֹת הַנְּפוּלוֹת

additions.reason: Line 2 states that the fallen fears ARE a bechina of the five terrors: 'וְהֵם בְּחִינַת (שבת עז:): חָמֵשׁ אֵימוֹת' — the intimidation of the weak over the strong. These are the five specific paradoxical fear-inversions (e.g., the small fish terrifying the large; the serpent over the lion). They represent the fallen form of the five gevurot, now operating as irrational terrors in the world. They are the external manifestation of יִרְאוֹת נְפוּלוֹת. Polarity evil because these terrors are the fallen, distorted form of divine gevurah.
additions.source_quote: וְהֵם בְּחִינַת (שבת עז:): חָמֵשׁ אֵימוֹת, אֵימַת חַלָּשׁ עַל הַגִּבּוֹר

additions.reason: Line 3 states: 'וְעַל כֵּן הֵם בְּמִסְפָּר חָמֵשׁ, כְּנֶגֶד חָמֵשׁ גְּבוּרוֹת' — the five fears correspond structurally to the five gevurot (divine powers of judgment/strength). The five gevurot are the positive root: they are the upper gevurot that become the five double letters מַנְצְפַ"ךְ (the final letters). The relationship between חָמֵשׁ אֵימוֹת (evil/fallen) and חָמֵשׁ גְּבוּרוֹת (good/root) is the same evil-mirror structure the framework describes — the same five-fold force appears as holy gevurot from above and as fallen terrors below. Polarity good because the gevurot are the divine source.
additions.source_quote: וְעַל כֵּן הֵם בְּמִסְפָּר חָמֵשׁ, כְּנֶגֶד חָמֵשׁ גְּבוּרוֹת, שֶׁהֵם חָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת מַנְצְפַ"ךְ כְּפוּלִים

additions.reason: Line 3 explicitly identifies the five double letters מ-נ-צ-פ-ך (the sofit/final forms) as the bechina/expression of the five gevurot: 'שֶׁהֵם חָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת מַנְצְפַ"ךְ כְּפוּלִים'. These five letters are the encoded form of the gevurot in language. This is a bechina-level identity: the five final letters ARE the five gevurot. Polarity good — these are sacred letter-forms that are the imprint of divine strength. They are the same nature as חָמֵשׁ גְּבוּרוֹת and belong in the same package.
additions.source_quote: כְּנֶגֶד חָמֵשׁ גְּבוּרוֹת, שֶׁהֵם חָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת מַנְצְפַ"ךְ כְּפוּלִים

additions.reason: Line 4 states: 'מְקוֹם הַיִּרְאָה הִיא בַּלֵּב' — the place (root) of fear is in the heart. Rashi is quoted to establish this: 'דָּבָר הַמָּסוּר לְלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ וְיָרֵאתָ'. Line 5 doubles down: 'עִקַּר הַדַּעַת – כְּשֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב' — the essential daat is when it is in the heart. The heart is the structural location shared by both yirah and daat — they are co-rooted there. The lev is the point of union where yirah and daat meet, producing true יִרְאַת ה' (line 6, Mishlei 2:5). Polarity good — the heart as the proper seat of yirah is a positive concept; it is where the elevation of fallen fears must arrive.
additions.source_quote: מְקוֹם הַיִּרְאָה הִיא בַּלֵּב; עִקַּר הַדַּעַת – כְּשֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב

additions.reason: Line 5 establishes that yirah must be accompanied by daat: 'הַיִּרְאָה צְרִיכָה לִהְיוֹת עִם דַּעַת, כִּי בְּלֹא דַּעַת נֶאֱמַר: הֲלֹא יִרְאָתְךָ כִּסְלָתֶךָ'. Without daat, fear becomes foolishness. The verse 'וְלֹא נָתַן לָכֶם לֵב לָדַעַת' uses לֵב לָדַעַת as a compound — the heart-for-knowing. The bechina relationship is: daat in the heart is the precondition for true yirah. Daat and yirah are structurally parallel as the two qualities that must both be seated in the lev. When they are combined (line 6), the verse confirms: 'אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה' וְדַעַת אֱלֹקִים תִּמְצָא'. Polarity good.
additions.source_quote: הַיִּרְאָה צְרִיכָה לִהְיוֹת עִם דַּעַת; הַדַּעַת צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בַּלֵּב

additions.reason: Line 9 identifies יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת as the positive apex of the Torah's teaching: when the din above is lifted, the person has nothing to fear except this — the transcendent awe of God's exaltedness. 'אֵין לוֹ רַק יִרְאָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת'. This is the elevated form of yirah that was the source of the fallen fears (the upper yirah that descended and clothed itself in worldly terrors). Yirat haromemut is bechina-parallel to יִרְאָה (the Torah's core concept) — it is what yirah IS in its proper state, in contrast to יִרְאוֹת נְפוּלוֹת which is what yirah becomes when it falls. This is the dominant positive concept of Package 1. Polarity good.
additions.source_quote: אֵין לוֹ רַק יִרְאָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת

additions.reason: Line 7-8 defines mishpat as the mechanism that elevates yirah: 'מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אֶרֶץ, הַיְנוּ עַל־יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט מַעֲמִיד וּמַעֲלֶה הַיִּרְאָה'. Mishpat — the practice of self-judgment, a person judging himself before Heaven judges him — is the tool that raises fallen fears back to their root. In the dataset, mishpat already appears as node1_id 'משפט' in eitza edges 445 and 1394 (both reference=154). It is therefore already in the dataset as a node but has NO bechina edges for Torah 154 and is not assigned to any Torah-154 package. The Torah itself uses 'הַיְנוּ' language — 'הַיְנוּ עַל־יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט' — which is definitional. Polarity good.
additions.source_quote: מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אֶרֶץ, הַיְנוּ עַל־יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט מַעֲמִיד וּמַעֲלֶה הַיִּרְאָה
additions.in_dataset_note: Node 'משפט' appears in eitza edges 445 and 1394 for Torah 154. It is NOT currently assigned to any Torah-154 package because no bechina edge connects it. The eitza relationship (mishpat LEADS TO elevated yirah) is correct — mishpat is a causal mechanism, not a bechina parallel of yirah. Therefore mishpat should NOT be merged into Package 1 by bechina. However, it must be recognized as a named concept in Torah 154 that is the operative eitza node between packages. If a second package is ever proposed for Torah 154 (see torah_154_new_packages.json), mishpat would anchor it.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Lines 1 and 8 mention yisurin (sufferings) and dinim (judgments) as what result from fallen fears, and 'דִּין שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה' (heavenly judgment) as what the person escapes through self-judgment. These appear in eitza edge 2170 (מה שהוא בעצמו שופט את עצמו → נצול מדין שלמעלה) as result-nodes. They are eitza outcomes, not bechina-parallel concepts. The source text does not use בְּחִינַת language for them. Excluded as eitza nodes only.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: מֶלֶךְ (king) from verse 'מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אֶרֶץ'
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 7 quotes the verse 'מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אֶרֶץ' (Mishlei 29). The Rebbe immediately interprets it: 'הַיְנוּ עַל־יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט מַעֲמִיד'. The 'king' in the verse is used to introduce the mishpat concept — it is the subject of the verse, not a bechina node in this Torah. The Rebbe does not say anything is a bechina of 'melekh' here. Excluded.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: יִרְאַת ה' from verse 'אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה' וְדַעַת אֱלֹקִים תִּמְצָא'
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 6 quotes Mishlei 2:5. 'יִרְאַת ה'' here is the named result of combining daat + yirah in the heart — it is the output of the equation. This is an eitza outcome (combining → produces yirat Hashem). However, it is essentially the same concept as 'יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת' — the elevated, proper fear. Not treated as a separate additional node since יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת in line 9 is the fuller explicit statement.
Mentioned as a negative contrast — even a non-Jew has daat, but without the heart. This is an example/contrast, not a bechina node. Excluded.

Line 9 uses both 'יִרְאָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה' and 'יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת' as synonymous descriptors of the same final state. Since יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת is more specific and explicit, it is proposed as the canonical node. יִרְאָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה is treated as an alias/variant of the same concept, not a separate addition.
